title: Hypatia Capital outbound scratchpad
content:
Quick personal scratchpad for outbound / intro to Hypatia Capital (private equity, fintech ops). Mostly notes to self + email/call drafts. Keep messy.

Account snapshot:
- Company: Hypatia Capital (mid-market PE firm, 400 employees globally, 3 portfolio tech companies in payments/credit scoring)
- HQ: NYC, engineering hubs in London + Bangalore
- Why they might care: portfolio companies run latency-sensitive ML scoring + embedding search for fraud/risk. High per-token cost on current hosted vendor, inconsistent latencies during peak batch scoring.
- Recent signal: job posting for "ML infra lead" (embedding infra + model serving) + talk at MoneyTech 2026 about reducing inference cost. Likely evaluating inference vendors or building in-house.
- Primary contact (target): Claire Donovan, Head of Platform Engineering (linkedin: claire-donovan-hypatia) — introduced tentatively via mutual connection (Aisha knows ex-colleague).
- Secondary contact: Ravi Menon, CTO (portfolio ops), and Priya Sethi, ML Engineering Manager at their payments portfolio company.

Hypotheses to test on intro call:
1) They have mixed deployment needs: some portfolio apps need hosted API during dev/experiments, others need private deployments for regulatory/data sensitivity.
2) Cost control and predictable latency are top 2 priorities. They will respond to hard metrics (p50/p95 latency, $/1000 tokens) + case studies.
3) They'll ask about model compatibility (LLMs + custom finetuned models) and KV-cache support for low-latency scoring.

Discovery questions (short list to surface pain):
- Current vendor stack for inference? (in-house, vendor, cloud endpoints)
- Monthly inference volume (tokens / embeddings) and distribution (real-time vs batch)?
- Biggest pain: cost, latency spikes, reliability, or model governance?
- Any regulatory/regulatory constraints for data residency or KMS/HSM requirements?
- Are they using any quantized models in prod (8-bit/4-bit) or exploring?
- How do they measure model quality/regressions today? prompts / eval sets?

Technical fit notes (things to mention / probe):
- Redwood strengths relevant to Hypatia: Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput), Private deployments (VPC/air-gapped), smart routing + fallbacks (keep scoring online during outages), prefix/KV caching for scoring use-cases.
- Quantization + kernel selection reduces GPU $/token; we should prepare ballpark numbers vs typical single-GPU cloud infra.
- If they care about embeddings: mention per-embedding throughput and ability to autoscale for batch async jobs (cost controls).

Outbound email drafts (A/B) - short and to the point. Pick 1-2 variants to test.
A) Subject: Cut inference costs + stabilize latency across portfolio
Hi Claire —
I saw Hypatia posted an ML infra lead and your MoneyTech talk — congrats. A quick note: we help platform teams at PE-backed fintechs standardize inference so portfolio apps get predictable latency and materially lower $/token (dedicated GPU pools + smart batching/caching).
If you have 15 minutes next week I can share a side-by-side of what we see customers saving vs managed cloud endpoints and a short checklist to decide hosted vs private deployment.
Best,
Jamie

B) Subject: Idea — keep real-time scoring fast during peak spikes
Claire —
Hypatia’s payments portfolio probably sees bursty scoring patterns. We built a small playbook that reduces p95 latency spikes using prefix caching + fallback model variants — customers cut p95 by ~30–50% in production. Interested in a quick call to run this playbook against a sample workload?

Call script (first 8 minutes):
- 0:00–0:30 quick intro + mutual intro (Aisha connection)
- 0:30–2:00 context: "Tell me about the scoring stack and where latency kills you"
- 2:00–5:00 probe volume/SLAs, regulatory constraints, current vendor costs
- 5:00–8:00 value props + example: "We recently helped a payments stack reduce inference spend 40% while removing p95 spikes by introducing dedicated pools + KV cache — would that matter here?"

Common objections + quick rebuttals (bullet form):
- "We already built something in-house." -> A: "Totally hear that. Many platform teams start in-house; main differentiation is operational cost and ongoing maintenance. We can run a 2-week proof-of-concept on a representative endpoint so you get apples-to-apples operational numbers (latency, cost, ops overhead)."
- "We're worried about vendor lock / data leakage." -> A: "Redwood offers private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and integrates with customer KMS/HSM. We can demo an air-gapped flow and provide SOC2/ISO artifacts. Also supportive of exportable configs / model artifacts so you keep control."
- "Pricing sounds complicated." -> A: "We standardize price vs per-token + optional reserved capacity. For Dedicated customers we model unit economics (tokens, throughput, GPU hours) and can show a forecast for 6–12 months. Bring a recent bill and we’ll model it live."

Experiment ideas / A/B to run with outreach:
- A: send short metric-driven email (savings + p95 stat)
- B: send use-case driven email (playbook for bursty scoring)
- C: invite to a 20-minute "Inference Ops Clinic" for PE-backed fintechs (hosted webinar) — measure conversions from A/B.

Metrics to try and capture if we get a POC:
- baseline p50/p95 latency (ms) for scoring endpoints
- token/embedding counts per month and per-hour peak throughput
- current $/month for inference (if available) and expected growth rate
- ops time spent on model rollouts and incident recovery (hours/month)

Legal / compliance flags to surface early:
- Data residency for EU clients — some portfolio companies operate in EU; will need VPC/on-prem or dedicated EU region
- KMS/HSM integration, audit logs need to be accessible to their compliance team
- Contracting lead time — private deployments often need legal + security review; surface early.

Next steps (if Claire responds positively):
1) Request one-hour working session with Priya (payments ML lead) and platform eng (Claire) — bring sample inference traces and a billing snapshot (high-level).
2) Run a lightweight smoke POC: 2 weeks, single endpoint, compare latency & $/token vs their current stack.
3) If POC looks good -> propose Dedicated pilot (1–3 GPU cluster) and optional private control plane for sensitive workloads.

TODOs for me:
- Aisha: ask for brief intro note to Claire (done? ping).
- Marco: prepare 1-pager comparing Redwood Dedicated vs typical cloud endpoint cost for embedding-heavy workload (target numbers: 30k embeddings/hr, 200 req/s peak).
- Legal: grab SOC2/ISO doc links and HSM/KMS checklist for attachments.
- Create a slide with p50/p95 improvements + example $/1M tokens savings to attach to first reply.

Notes to self (random):
- Keep email <120 words. If they open but don't respond, follow up with an example cost-savings table.
- For POC, prefer to run against a non-prod dataset or sampled traces to avoid legal delays.
- If they push for price up-front, offer a templated modeling session instead of a number.

Rough past-customer reference to mention if asked:
- "We worked with QuantaPay (payments stack) to move scoring off a spot-based self-hosted infra to a dedicated Redwood pool — result: 40% lower inference spend and 35% fewer incidents due to consistent p95."

End of scratchpad. Keep this version private. Update after intro call and move to shared_drive if we spin up a POC.
